newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-KIPKETER CONTINUES TO SPEAK IN CIRCLES.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KIPKETER CONTINUES TO SPEAK IN CIRCLES.

text.p: Wilson Kipketer runs in circles for a living. Most interviews with the co-holder of the world 800 metres record travel in the same direction.
The Kenyan-born Dane is the overwhelming favourite to win another world championship gold here and possibly break the world record he shares with Seb Coe.
Yet Kipketer seldom offers direct answers to reporters inquiring about his running talents or private life.
Even inquiries of how fast he would like to run are skilfully dodged.

"Yes, I have (a dream)," the 24-year-old Kipketer said at a news conference sponsored by his shoe company on Sunday. "But I cannot tell you because it is my personal dream. I will tell you when I reached my goal."
So intrigued - or frustrated - did one journalist become after 30 minutes of bantering with Kipketer that he suggested the runner might have overwhelming in a different profession.
"Have you every considered being a lawyer?" the reporter asked.
"I have no answer," said Kipketer. "Ask me in five years' time."

By then Kipketer could be looking for new challenges. He certainly has few over 800 metres, where other runners attempt to treat him, as Dutch competitor Marko Koers said, "as a human" but seldom can".

Twice during March's world indoor championships Kipketer bettered the indoor world record. Then last month he equalled Coe's outdoor record of one minute 41.73 seconds with an awesome kick at Stockholm after hope for a record appeared lost.
No matter what the pace, Kipketer seems to win.
"He's the gold medallist already," proclaimed pole vault world record holder Sergei Bubka.
Asked to respond, Kipketer reminded his audience that there would be 61 other athletes in the 800 metres, whose preliminaries begin on Monday.
"We have to qualify and play the game," said Kipketer.
It is a skill Kipketer knows well whether on the track or in the interview room.
